To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following variables are significant in predicting the time required to complete a software maintenance task: program size, control-flow complexity, time pressure, and the interaction of program size and time pressure.

the amount of time it takes to make a change to a software program is affected by the complexity of the program, the complexity of the change, and the amount of knowledge the person making the change has of the program and the change to be made.
the effects of program complexity and semantic knowledge are moderated by time pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the impact of individual and program attributes on software maintenance effort and with identifying those factors which can lead to more effective and efficient software maintenance practices.
the development and evaluation of a theory of the impact of the interaction between individual and task characteristics on maintenance effort and performance.

the development of a framework for understanding how individual differences in information processing capability and the characteristics of the task interact in determining the effort required by software maintenance personnel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a HIP perspective can serve as a valuable framework for examining the impact of individual and program characteristics on maintenance effort.

the results of this experiment support the hypothesis that an individual's information-processing capabilities and characteristics of the program to be maintained interact to determine the time required for the maintenance activity.

the results of the experiment support the notion that the HIP model can serve as an effective framework for understanding the interaction of individual, task, and environmental characteristics on software maintenance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HIP framework is an effective tool for understanding and predicting software maintenance performance.

we have developed a framework for understanding the impact of individual and task variables on software maintenance performance, and we have developed a tool for empirically investigating this impact.
the experimental results support the use of an individual's cognitive capability as an explanatory variable in the study of the software maintenance process.

the human factor is an important component of software maintenance.
the HIP model is a viable framework for studying the impact of individual characteristics and task complexity on software maintenance effort.
